purpose: Cross-check BFAR Region II NIFEP lake names Casili Lake and Bayo/Bayolake against independent inland-water and local-government evidence; search for site-specific fish evidence without inferring from program-level stocking or unrelated waterbodies.

programEvidence.reportedStatus: 2018 report says restored and enhanced in 2016

independentLocalityEvidence.organismGroup: freshwater cladoceran microcrustacean; not a fish

coordinateLead.useLimit: Historical lake-level point for cross-check only; not a fish event coordinate or shoreline polygon.

candidateWaterbodies.identityDecision: The shared Tuao/Cagayan locality and Cassily/Casili spellings make Lake Cassily a plausible crosswalk candidate for NIFEP Casili Lake, but no reviewed source directly states that these are the same waterbody. Keep formal identity unresolved pending a site map or direct LGU/BFAR confirmation.
candidateWaterbodies.fishEvidence: No site-specific fish survey or checklist was retrieved in bounded official-source searches. This is a retrieval gap, not evidence that fish or surveys are absent.

programEvidence.reportedStatus: 2018 report says restored and enhanced in 2016

candidateWaterbodies.nameCrosswalk: The same Iguig locality appears with Bayo Lake/Bayolake spellings across BFAR publications; treat this as a likely spelling/reporting variant for research triage while preserving each source spelling. Exact official name, waterbody identity and mapped footprint are not independently resolved.
candidateWaterbodies.fishEvidence: No site-specific fish survey or checklist was retrieved in bounded searches; the BFAR sources are program records, not taxon-by-site surveys.

programStockingContext.finding: The newsletter reports 5,000 mixed carp-species and tilapia fingerlings at the separate 1-ha Quirino State University reservoir. In the same article, Bayo Lake and Casili Lake are named as other rehabilitation areas.
programStockingContext.doNotInfer: Do not transfer QSU reservoir taxa, quantity, catch or stocking event to Casili or Bayo Lake.

queries: site:region2.bfar.da.gov.ph "Casili Lake" fish OR "Bayo Lake" fisheries
site:repository.seafdec.org "Lake Cassily" fish OR "Casili Lake" fish
officialRepositorySearches.result: No site-specific fish survey or lake-specific fish checklist was retrieved in these bounded searches.
officialRepositorySearches.interpretation: Search/retrieval limitation only; it does not establish absence of fish, surveys or unpublished agency records.

boundedGbifScreen.interpretation: The 12 zero results apply only to exact indexed text in the queried fields with country=PH. They do not show species absence or absence of source records; alternate spelling, unindexed or blank locality fields and other datasets remain outside scope.

limits: A BFAR NIFEP restoration/enhancement entry is not a fish occurrence record or a current fish checklist.
The cladoceran locality and specimens are non-fish evidence; the exact sample collection year is unresolved in the article.
The published Cassily coordinate is a point without stated uncertainty and is not a boundary.
No source reviewed here provides a reusable polygon or a direct Casili↔Cassily or Bayo↔Bayolake official gazetteer crosswalk.
Reuse conditions for the scientific paper and BFAR source materials have not been approved for app projection.
nextAction: Seek NIFEP completion records/site maps for Casili and Bayo, then find corresponding lake-specific fishery assessments, stocking inventories and voucher records. Ask for UST-ZRC field metadata to resolve the Cassily sample year and locality. Keep each fish list separate by waterbody and wild-versus-stocked provenance.
